newsitem.title: UK: Bookies expecct even higher Halifax share price.
newsitem.headline: Bookies expecct even higher Halifax share price.

text.p: The grey market in Halifax Building Society shares rose to new heights on Wednesday, with London financial bookmakers quoting the closing price on its first day of trading at 740-750 pence.
"We have been trading the market for over two weeks and all we have seen are bulls, with buyers outnumbering sellers by 10 to one," Dave Morrison of City Index said in a statement.

Halifax, Britain's largest mortgage lender, is expected to convert to a publicly listed company on Monday June 2. On Tuesday it said 23 percent of its flotation shares would be sold by members in an initial auction to institutional shareholders.
"After the success of the Alliance & Leicester flotation, our clients are expecting Halifax shares to close over seven pounds. Our current quotation is 7.40-7.50 pounds ($12.23)," he added.
In January, the Halifax estimated its shares would be priced at between 390 and 450 pence. Last month it set a 415 pence floor value on the shares sold via its free dealing service on flotation.

Around two-thirds of Halifax members -- the savers and borrowers with the mutual building society -- will receive the basic 200 shares windfall. They will receive additional shares based on their levels of savings.
At the top of City Index's levels, the average payout to Halifax's members would be around 2,300 pounds, around 1000 pounds more than the society's initial forecast in January.

This would also value the group, which is ditching its mutual status in favour of the public flotation and joining the ranks of Britain's banks, at nearly 19.0 billion pounds and rank it among Britain's top-ten largest companies. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
